activities.title: Student Profile Card guided Build

contract.doing: Create a `student-profile` folder with `profile.c` and `evidence.md`. The program stores an integer student ID, integer weekly minutes, double planned hours, and one char study level, then prints a five-line card. Compile as C17 with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`, run the exact executable, and repair two deliberate compiler findings without adding input, branches, loops, or calculator behavior.

contract.output: A `student-profile` folder containing warning-free profile.c and evidence.md that reproduces the build, run, warning repair, and syntax repair.

activities.title: Practical Exam Eligibility Checker guided Build

contract.doing: Create `exam-eligibility/eligibility.c`. Read three integers: registered flag (0 or 1), classes held (1–200), and classes attended (0 through held). Reject incomplete scans and invalid ranges before calculating attendance. A learner is eligible only when registered equals 1 and attendance is at least 75.0 percent.
contract.why: Practical exams often require several rules at once; reliable C code must reject impossible state before arithmetic and keep invalid input separate from a valid not-eligible result.
contract.output: A six-case eligibility checker with a proven zero-divisor guard and truth-table-led logical-operator repair.
contract.tools: Windows, MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC/GDB, VS Code, PowerShell, and the C standard library
contract.prerequisites: Previously completed competencies: CLNG-R2-C005, CLNG-R2-C006. New Week concepts are taught in Core Study before this Build.
contract.finished: Every incomplete or out-of-range input stops with the documented error before attendance calculation. Classes held equal to zero is rejected without division. Exactly 75.0 percent is eligible when registered; a lower result is not eligible. An unregistered learner remains not eligible even with 100 percent attendance. Each supplied case prints exactly one terminal result. The &&/|| defect is explained with actual truth values and repaired without changing unrelated branches.
contract.submission: Written branch order and six-case expected-versus-actual table | Zero-held result proving no percentage calculation ran | 75-percent and registration boundary results | &&/|| truth table, defect result, repair, and full rerun

activities.title: Persistent Study Log guided Build

contract.doing: Create `study-log/` with `main.c`, `study_log.c`, `study_log.h`, and `checks.c`. Store up to 20 records as `id|minutes|subject`, where id is positive, minutes is 1–600, subject is nonempty and contains no pipe, and each line fits a 160-byte buffer. A missing `study-log.txt` begins empty; another open failure or any malformed existing line stops without writing. The normal add path appends one valid record.
contract.why: Useful programs survive restarts, but safe persistence means a malformed or unreadable existing file must never be mistaken for empty state and overwritten.
contract.output: A six-check persistent study log with a debugger record and byte-preservation evidence for malformed storage.

The normal append remains after restart and receives a unique positive ID. The debugger record shows the failing values before the one-cause repair. All six named checks pass warning-free and the malformed-file before/after comparison matches.
